edges.notes: OverlayFS is a Linux kernel filesystem implementation (overlay) for stacked lower/upper directory trees per kernel documentation.
Overlay mounts are scoped by mount namespaces; union mounts are not namespace types themselves.
OCI image layers describe content addressing and manifests; overlay mounts are one common Linux materialization strategy, not the spec itself.
OCI runtime bundles define container filesystem roots; runtimes may use overlay mounts on Linux to assemble roots, distinct from the spec text.
Docker on Linux commonly uses overlay storage drivers backed by the kernel overlay filesystem per common deployment understanding.
containerd snapshotters may assemble container root filesystems using overlay mounts on Linux.
runc starts bundles on Linux where the prepared rootfs may be produced via overlay mounts by higher layers.
Podman storage on Linux frequently uses overlay-style filesystem assembly for containers.
CRI-O uses Linux storage backends that may compose overlay mounts for Kubernetes pod filesystems.
Kubernetes node runtimes rely on Linux filesystem assembly strategies; overlay is common but not universal.
OverlayFS is an in-kernel stacked filesystem; FUSE delegates filesystem work to userspace — distinct mechanisms.
